chapter: Harlem, 52nd Street and the first big bands
title: Racial mixing at the Famous Door and Onyx Club, and the big bands there
summary: Management attitudes varied by club; Barnet says Basie was first big band at the Famous Door, he was second, followed by Woody Herman and others.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Even on 52nd Street, or especially on 52nd Street, or how --

Well, now, it depended on the bosses. I mean, you'd get right down to it. I mean like Joe Helblock, next door at the Onyx Club, was very liberally minded. There wasn't any problem there. Whereas, at the Famous Door, where both of these incidents took place, the management there wasn't, while they employed black orchestras, they apparently didn't want anybody to mix up. I did not have a mixed band in there. And of course that was -- we're going way ahead of it. We're getting up -- but although -- I think it had to do with the place, because I was able to get away with it up in the Park Central Hotel and the Cocoanut Grove, and yet these things happened in a little joint on 52nd Street.
But on 52nd Street, at the Famous Door, you weren't allowed to? You just didn't happen to have or you were not allowed to have a mixed band?
I didn't happen to have one.
Oh. But if you had wanted to could you have, do you think, or do you know?
I don't know. I really don't. I think that I could have gotten away with it. Because I think those guys that ran that place, I mean if you were doing business

and the band was good, I don't think they cared. As long as the people were coming in. But as far as, you know, consorting with people that were working there, they took a dim view of that. This was before they had the big bands. This was the time like when the Louis Prima band was playing in there. This was before they went to the large bands in there. Of course Basie was the first one there with the big band, and I was the second, and then I think Woody Herman came in, and then there was a whole slew, Teddy Powell, and even Red Nichols.
Well, I mean you don't normally think of him with a big band.
But he did have one in there. Oh, and then the Will Bradley band. They worked there.
